result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is the better team document: it ties the main message to the dial-and-paper-log habit, sets plain wording rules ('laid out like,' never 'accepted by'), and is more specific about what proof to gather (county confirmation, how often the hub is needed, alerts and product saved). Its bracketed placeholders make it a little less finished, and it merges creameries and butchers into one buyer version. A is clean and complete, but its buyer versions are thin, and it adds unsupported inferences such as 'many creameries have metal walk-ins' and 'roughly six months.' | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers are complete, stay mostly within the fact sheet and state the awkward bits plainly. B's buyer versions are more distinct: butchers get their own section tied to the dial thermometer, and caterers are tied to the clipboard. B's 'if they ask' table, which includes the full cost with the hub, is also ready to use with buyers, and its 150-word bio differs more from the 60-word one. A has a stronger list of proof still needed, including county confirmation and how often walk-ins need the hub, but it leaves bracketed placeholders in the doc. B adds small inferences of its own: 'many creameries have metal walk-ins' and a pilot of 'roughly six months'.
